scribe.question: A page header appears on every page of a three-page document. What does scribe do with it?

options.text: Removes it, because it repeats on most pages
Keeps it, because it is real text
Keeps the first one and removes the rest
Turns it into a heading

scribe.question: The word "well-being" is split across two lines as "well-" then "being". What does scribe produce?

options.text: wellbeing, with the hyphen removed
well-being, with the hyphen kept
well- being, with the line break still there
well being, with both the hyphen and line break removed

scribe.question: What does scribe do with page numbers?

options.text: Removes them along with other page furniture
Keeps them at the bottom of each page
Moves them to the end of the document
Turns them into section numbers

scribe.question: A heading like "3.1 Sites" appears on most pages of a document. What happens to it?

options.text: It is removed as page furniture, because it repeats on most pages
It is kept as a heading, because it is numbered
The first one is kept and the repeats are removed
It is kept, because furniture removal happens after heading detection

scribe.question: A one-page document has a header at the top. Can scribe detect and remove it?

options.text: No, because the header needs to repeat across pages to be detected
Yes, because it is at the top of the page
Yes, if you tell scribe what to remove
No, because one-page documents are not supported

tally.question: You bought the same £3 coffee twice on the same day at the same shop. What does the summary show?

options.text: One, because the two rows look identical and one is treated as a duplicate
Both, because they are two separate purchases
Both, with the second one flagged as a possible duplicate
Neither, because duplicates are removed entirely

tally.question: You move £300 from your current account to your savings account. How does tally treat this?

options.text: Leaves it out, because it is a transfer, not spending
Counts it as spending in a transfers category
Counts it as spending, because it left the current account
Asks you whether to include it

tally.question: You make a payment on the last day of January. The bank processes it on the first day of February. Which month does the summary put it in?

options.text: January, because tally uses the date you made the payment
February, because tally uses the date the bank processed it
Both months, split equally
Whichever month the bank says

tally.question: A shop name does not match anything on the list. What happens to that payment?

options.text: It goes under uncategorised
It is left out of the summary
Tally stops and reports an error
It is put in the category closest to its name

tally.question: The list of shop names is written into the code. What is the problem with that?

options.text: You have to change the code to add a new shop
The list cannot be shared with other people
The list is too slow to search
The list cannot handle shops with similar names
